messages.subject: error handling decision
parts:
I think we should

* configure error handling policy globally for all of
the functions in Stan (we can use Boost's global policy
or customize it in a single location)

* remove function signatures with explicit Policy
template parameters & use global values

Step 2 cuts the number of function definitions in half
without invoking C++-11-only function template defaults.

I think we should also:

* remove implicit propto=false probabilty functions and
require explicit template parameter instantiation

The model code is already making propto specific, e.g. with
normal_log<false>(...).

Step 2 and 3 together take us back to one C++ templated
function signature per Stan function signature. There may be
more than one implementation because of specializations for
auto-dif.

The change should be relatively easy and modular because
we'd be removing functionality we haven't used.

Let's finalize a decision in the meeting tomorrow.

- Bob

messages.author: cab04b8f0759c712
messages.subject: Re: [stan-dev] error handling decision
parts: Bob, thanks for getting these thoughts out. I'm inlining some thoughts.

On Mon, Apr 1, 2013 at 1:03 PM, Bob Carpenter <ca...@alias-i.com> wrote:
I think we should

  * configure error handling policy globally for all of
    the functions in Stan (we can use Boost's global policy
    or customize it in a single location)

That works for me. It will disable our ability to use policies to disable specific error checking in things like distributions calling other distributions, but I'm ok with this decision because it will simplify our code greatly. That and we haven't really had a need for configurable error handling.

* remove function signatures with explicit Policy
    template parameters & use global values

Step 2 cuts the number of function definitions in half
without invoking C++-11-only function template defaults.
Yeah, that sounds good. It'll be easier to maintain and we can cut down on some of our tests.

I think we should also:

  * remove implicit propto=false probabilty functions and
    require explicit template parameter instantiation

Yes! For those of you not following closely, this will change the C++ calls a little. This means calling normal_log(y, mu, sigma) will require a call like:
normal_log<true,true,true>(y, mu, sigma). This way we can drop appropriate proportionality constants in a more controlled fashion from the outside.

I'm not sure if the logic we used for determining when to compute gradients will still hold, but it's just a thought exercise that we need to walk through once, I think.

The model code is already making propto specific, e.g. with
normal_log<false>(...).

Step 2 and 3 together take us back to one C++ templated
function signature per Stan function signature.  There may be
more than one implementation because of specializations for
auto-dif.

The change should be relatively easy and modular because
we'd be removing functionality we haven't used.
Agreed. A little bit of work, but easy.
Let's finalize a decision in the meeting tomorrow.

Unless someone has a compelling reason against doing this, my vote is for the suggestions that Bob has laid out.

 
- Bob
